endorsements.quote: Engaging PwMS in the co-design of algorithms, feature selection, and usability testing ensures greater trust and adoption of AI solutions [ 81 ].
Regular and transparent evaluation of AI tools within real-world clinical settings is crucial.
Furthermore, explainable AI (XAI) principles foster transparency, enabling clinicians to make informed decisions rather than relying solely on opaque “black-box” predictions [ 61 , 85 ].

unlisted_practices: Adopt consistent data structures such as FHIR and OMOP common data models in hospital EHR systems to standardise MS data collection across sites.
Complement federated learning pipelines with standardised data schemas, ontologies and harmonised semantic structures.
Use regulatory sandboxes for supervised co-design and testing of high-risk AI tools by developers, clinicians and regulators before formal deployment.
Establish structured post-market surveillance and continuous real-world evaluation of AI tools aligned with regulatory guidelines.
Fund publicly available open-source toolkits, multilateral financing and global minimum-dataset standards so AI solutions remain affordable and interoperable across economic settings.
Involve patients and advocacy groups in defining relevant outcomes, dataset priorities and design decisions for AI tools.

screen.reason: This is a perspective/commentary paper discussing challenges, regulatory/ethical frameworks, and recommendations for integrating big data and AI for multiple sclerosis progression prediction.
